route_markers.name: Alto del Desierto de las Palmas
route_markers.label: Climb — Cat 2

guideposts.label: Memories from Alcossebre (and Castello)
guideposts.detail: Alcossebre is a stage town for the second time in La Vuelta history. In 2017, it hosted the finish of stage 5 after a route that is almost the same as today’s, on the opposite direction. The stage started in Benicassim, passed Castello at km 8, and then faced the ascents of the Alto del Desierto de las Palmas, Alto de Cabanes, Cool de la Bandereta and Puerto de La Serratella, also featured on toda

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: UAE Emirates XRG still lead the team standings with a gap of 6’20’’ to Visma-Lease a Bike and 10’26’’ to Visma-Lease a Bike.

guideposts.label: Stage 6 is ON!
guideposts.detail: The riders canbattle it out in the province of Castellon, home to a La Vuelta stage for the first time since 2023, when Kaden Groves won in Borriana.

guideposts.label: First attacks...
guideposts.detail: But the bunch is packed at km 3.

guideposts.label: Already past Alcala de Xivert
guideposts.detail: Alcala de Xivert (km 6) is Vicente Iturat’s hometown, winner of 4 La Vuelta stages and the points standings 1957. It was also the finish of stage 7 of La Vuelta 1977, an edition outrageously dominated by Freddy Maertens: the Belgian icon was the overall leader from start to finish, with 13 stage wins.

guideposts.label: 8 riders on the move
guideposts.detail: The battle for the breakaway goes on after 10 kilometres of hard racing.

guideposts.label: All together at km 12
guideposts.detail: Many riders announced they wanted to break away today. "If the breakaway takes a lot of time to form, then it becomes less of a workload for UAE to control the race and then go for the stage win", Jack Haig (Netcompany Ineos) warns. "But I imagine probably a strong breakaway will go for the win today."

guideposts.label: Lutsenko on the move with Bisiaux
guideposts.detail: Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) and Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) set off from the bunch at km 16 and are riding a few metres ahead of the peloton. Meanwhile, Jay Vine (UAE Emirates XRG) returns to the bunch after a mechanical.

guideposts.label: 15 seconds at km 18
guideposts.detail: Alexey Lutsenko and Léo Bisiaux keep pushing.

guideposts.label: 7 chasers behind Lustenko and Bisiaux
guideposts.detail: The gap from the lead duo to the bunch is still 15 seconds. And there are seven chasers in between.

guideposts.label: The chasers are caught by the bunch
guideposts.detail: Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) and Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) still lead the way.

guideposts.label: 1 gap of 24'' at km 24
guideposts.detail: Lutsenko and Bisiaux pushed their lead up to 33'' but the battle goes on behind them.

guideposts.label: De la Cruz and Kron in pursuit
guideposts.detail: David de la Cruz (Pinarello Q36.5) and Andreas Kron (Uno-X Mobility) are chasing 25'' behind Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) and Alexey Lutsenko (NSN). The gap to the bunch: 31''.

guideposts.label: De la Cruz and Kron are caught
guideposts.detail: The gap to the lead duo is down to 20''.

guideposts.label: 30 kilometres of battle
guideposts.detail: Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) and Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) are 20 seconds ahead of the bunch. Walter Calzoni (Pinarello Q36.5) sets off in pursuit.

guideposts.label: Calzoni joins Bisiaux and Lutsenko
guideposts.detail: The peloton are right behind the lead trio.

guideposts.label: The attackers are caught at km 33
guideposts.detail: They're at the bottom of the first categorised climb of the day, Puerto de la Serratella (14km at 3.8%).

guideposts.label: Attacks keep flying
guideposts.detail: Sixteen riders have just opened a small gap (km 36).

guideposts.label: Back together again
guideposts.detail: This is the most intense battle for the break so far at La Vuelta 26.

guideposts.label: 39.4 km in the first hour
guideposts.detail: The riders have already climbed 1,000 metres of elevation gain.

guideposts.label: The first climb is done
guideposts.detail: The attackers haven't managed to break away.

guideposts.label: Results at Puerto de la Serratella (cat. 2, km 44.6)
guideposts.detail: 1. Buitrago, 5 pts 2. Fortunato, 3 pts 3. Küng, 1 pt

guideposts.label: Joshua Tarling abandons La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: The British powerhouse was third in the opening stage in Monaco.

guideposts.label: Another move
guideposts.detail: Four riders have opened a gap. For how long?

guideposts.label: The attacekrs are caught again
guideposts.detail: The bunch is at km 58.

guideposts.label: 17 riders onthe move
guideposts.detail: They're about to tackle the second climb of the day.

guideposts.label: Back together again
guideposts.detail: The attackers are caught at km 63, on the ascent to Coll de la Bandereta.

guideposts.label: Bennett, Kron and Leemreize lead the way
guideposts.detail: They have opened a gap of 10 seconds.

guideposts.label: Buitrago sets off
guideposts.detail: The Colombian climber rapidly bridges the gap to the lead trio. The peloton trail by 14'' at the summit.

guideposts.label: Canal in pursuit
guideposts.detail: Carlos Canal (Movistar) is chasing 18'' behind the four leaders. The peloton trail by 27''.

guideposts.label: 10 chasers
guideposts.detail: The four leaders are about to enter the final 100 kilometres of the stage. Ten chasers trail by 18 seconds. The gap to the bunch is up to 35 seconds.

guideposts.label: Beloki has abandoned
guideposts.detail: Markel Beloki (EF Education-EasyPost) is the second rider out of La Vuelta 26 today, after Josh Tarling (Netcompany Ineos).

guideposts.label: The chasers are reeled in
guideposts.detail: The peloton are 30 seconds behind the leaders with 91 km to go.

guideposts.label: Heading for the main challenges of the day
guideposts.detail: The first challenges eventually saw 16 riders break away. Now they make their way to Benicassim, to face two ascents on the same slopes. The Alto del Desierto de las Palmas is an emblematic ascent in the are. It will be summited a first time with 48.9 km to go, after a 7.6 km ascent at 4.9%. Then, the peloton will return to Benicassim and tackle the ascent again. But they will continue climbing al

guideposts.label: Memories from Benicassim
guideposts.detail: Passed twice on today’s course (km 117 and 141.8), Benicassim first hosted La Vuelta stage in 1969 (stage 8), with Spain’s Ramon Saez taking the win ahead of the overall leader, Belgium’s Raymond Steegmans. Benicassim hosted the Gran Salida in 1990 with an ITT wonky Pello Ruiz Cabestany. Benicassim is also a classic venue for local events such as the Volta a la Comunitat Valencia.

guideposts.label: 2 minutes
guideposts.detail: The 16 attackers are 65 km from the finish. The peloton trail by 2'03''.

guideposts.label: 6 Grand Tour stage winners in the breakaway
guideposts.detail: 14 stage wins - Wout van Aert (Tour de France x10, La Vuelta x3, Giro d'Italia x1) 3 - Pello Bilbao (Giro d'Italia x2, Tour de France x1) 2 - Santiago Buitrago (Giro d'Italia x2) 1 - Patrick Konrad (Tour de France x1) 1 - Urko Berrade (La Vuelta x1) 1 - Andreas Kron (La Vuelta x1)

guideposts.label: Van Aert is dropped from the breakaway
guideposts.detail: The attackers are less than 5 kilometres from the summit. Bilbao sets the pace. The last gap to the bunch: 2'27''

guideposts.label: Diaz accelerates
guideposts.detail: The Spanish climber opens a gap into the last kilometre of ascent. The average speed after three hours: 42.3 km/h.

guideposts.label: Resultats at Alto del Desierto de las Palmas (cat. 2, km 128)
guideposts.detail: 1. Diaz, 5 pts 2. Buitrago, 3 pts 3. Gloag, 1pt

guideposts.label: The gap has decreased on the downhill
guideposts.detail: The attackers return to the valley with a lead of 2'10''. The riders who were dropped on the ascent have returned to the front except for Van Aert.

guideposts.label: The situation stabilises on the valley
guideposts.detail: The leaders are 5 kilometres away from the final climb. The peloton trail by 2'00''.

guideposts.label: Bilbao is dropped from the lead group
guideposts.detail: The Spaniard pulled to try and give Buitrago a shot at the stage win today. The gap is down to 1'25''.

guideposts.label: Craps and Kron up the ante
guideposts.detail: Buitrago chases them down 7 km from the summit. The breakaway explodes.

guideposts.label: Debruyne and Pogacar increase the pace
guideposts.detail: The gap is down to 30 seconds with 4 km left of climbing.

guideposts.label: Pogacar catches and drops Debruyne
guideposts.detail: They are just inside the last 3 kilometres of ascent.

guideposts.label: Mas catches Pogacar
guideposts.detail: They're at the summit. The Spaniard goes first.

guideposts.label: Results at Puerto El Bartolo (cat. 1, km 156.3)
guideposts.detail: 1. Mas, 10 pts / 6'' 2. Pogacar, 6 pts / 4'' 3. Gall, 4 pts / 2'' 4. Roglic, 2 pts 5. Debruyne, 1 pt

guideposts.label: 12 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: The situation remains unchanged on the downhill.

guideposts.label: Tejada attacks from the chase group
guideposts.detail: Gall drives the chase. They are still 30 seconds behind the lead duo, who have entered the final 3 kilometres. +1'35'' Onley - Kuss group

guideposts.label: Tadej Pogacar wins stage 6 of La Vuelta 26!
guideposts.detail: Already his third stage win in this edition!

guideposts.label: Top 5
guideposts.detail: 1. Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) 2. Enric Mas (Movistar) 3. Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech), +46'' 4. Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) 5. Harold Tejada (XDS Astana)
